title: Declare the psycopg v3 production runtime dependency
intent: Install the driver selected by production postgresql+psycopg DATABASE_URL values so the API can import its required auth router and start on Railway.
behavior_change: Fresh API installs include psycopg v3 in addition to the existing psycopg2 driver; database URLs, pooling, queries, schemas, and application code remain unchanged.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Added psycopg[binary] for SQLAlchemy's postgresql+psycopg dialect and a focused subprocess smoke test that imports app.db.session with that production URL shape without opening a database connection.
diff_articulation.why: The reliable-elegance Railway backend repeatedly crashes during auth_router import because app.db.session constructs the production engine with postgresql+psycopg while clean installs contain only psycopg2-binary.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: psycopg2-binary provides the psycopg2 module used directly by app.core.rmos_db; it does not provide the psycopg module selected by SQLAlchemy's psycopg dialect. Both declarations have live consumers.
diff_articulation.what_did_not_change: No driver replacement, database URL rewrite, SQLAlchemy pin, connection attempt, pool implementation, route, schema, migration, or production configuration changed.
diff_articulation.why_structural_extraction: The dependency declaration owns runtime availability; changing application imports or rewriting Railway configuration would conceal the mismatch instead of declaring the capability already selected in production.

commands_run: Railway reliable-elegance logs reproduced ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg' during app.db.session engine construction
proofs: The production URL explicitly selects SQLAlchemy's psycopg v3 dialect.
The legacy RMOS store still imports psycopg2 directly, so its existing dependency remains intact.
The regression test constructs the same engine class used at API startup but never connects to PostgreSQL.
verification.hardware: No hardware or manufacturing output involved.

files.intent: Declare the psycopg v3 driver selected by the production SQLAlchemy URL.
files.behavior_change: Fresh installs include psycopg v3 and its binary distribution.

files.intent: Prevent production URL support from again depending on an undeclared database driver.

findings: LOW: the repository currently supports two synchronous PostgreSQL access paths with different driver generations; retaining both is the narrow compatibility repair, while consolidation is a separate architecture change.
architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: This hotfix declares the missing live capability and avoids changing either database consumer during deployment recovery.
